div.div: WE WRITE AN INGEST.PY FILE TO INGEST ALL THE LOGS FROM THE SERVER. WE CATER FOR:
SIMPLE VALIDATION FOR: EMPTY LOG FILE, INCORRECT LOG FORMAT - SO WE CAN SAFELY LOAD TO S3 - A STRUCTURALLY SOUND LOG FILE

div.div: THIS PIPELINE INGESTS SERVER LOGS FROM A SERVER.
- INGESTING LOGS FROM A SERVER THROUGH A NETWORK

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 148px; height: 1px; padding-top: 167px; margin-left: 313px;

div.div: WE LOAD RAW LOG FILE TO S3 - WE CREATE AN S3 BUCKET TO HOLD ALL LOG FILES PARTITIONED USING THE HIVE PARTITIONING FORMAT - STORE LOG FILES BY DAY (SCALE TO HOURLY STORAGE FOR LARGE AMOUNTS OF INCOMING LOGS PER HOUR)
- OUTCOME - AN S3 BUCKET WITH RAW LOG DATA PARTITIONED USING HIVE
WE INCLUDE S3 IN THIS PIPELINE BECAUSE WE NEED TO STORE RAW LOG FILES FOR PERSISTENCE AND HISTORICAL AUDITING

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 167px; height: 1px; padding-top: 167px; margin-left: 503px;

div.div: THIS IS WHERE THE MAGIC, ERRORS AND BUGS ALL LIVE - WE SEEK TO FLESH OUT A STRUCTURE OUT OF THE UNSTRUCTRED LOGS.
- WE USE REGEX AND FILE MATCHING PATTERNS TO FLESH OUT INDIVIDUAL EVENTS
- LOGS THAT DO NOT FOLLOW REQUIRED STRUCTURED ARE ACTUALLY LOGGED AND SAVED. WE DON'T DISCARD THEM BUT USE THE DEAD LETTER QUEUE APPROACH TO HANDLE THEM
- OUTCOME - A STRUCTURED DATASET WITH CLEARLY DEFINED ROWS AND COLUMNS
